display_name: Ibn Battuta & T.S. Burt in the Chandela Afterlife
one_line: A time-crossing duo of witnesses to Khajuraho and the Chandela landscape, meeting in a serene afterlife where they share what they saw of survival, ruin and rediscovery.

appearance.age_look: Ibn Battuta appears as a lean man in his mid-30s, T.S. Burt as a fit man in his early 40s; both athletic but not bulky, with upright, observant posture.
appearance.face: Ibn Battuta has an oval face, warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, trimmed pointed beard and mustache, sharp dark eyes and a calm, thoughtful default expression; Burt has a slightly longer, angular face with light brown complexion, neatly trimmed sideburns and jawline beard, blue-gray eyes and an intent, quietly curious default expression.
appearance.hair: Ibn Battuta’s hair is dark brown, mostly hidden under a soft white turban with a narrow deep-red band at the base; what shows at the sides is short and wavy; Burt has chestnut-brown hair swept back to mid-length at the nape, tidy but wind-ruffled, with a simple tan military forage cap in his left hand or tucked at his belt, not worn.
appearance.costume: Ibn Battuta wears a 14th-century Maghribi-Persian traveler’s outfit: a long, loose, cream-colored cotton jubba (robe) reaching mid-calf with a narrow stand collar and simple ties at the chest, layered over a light sky-blue long-sleeved tunic and dark brown narrow trousers; the jubba edges and cuffs have a thin deep-red piping; he has a wide dark-red woolen sash wrapped twice around his waist with the ends hanging to his left, and over his shoulders a light gray travel cloak folded back like a shawl; his feet are in sturdy brown leather sandals with simple straps, and he carries a small leather belt-pouch. Burt wears early-19th-century British East India Company field attire adapted for Bundelkhand: a light khaki cotton single-breasted frock coat with knee-length skirts, high stand collar and plain brass buttons, worn open over a crisp white shirt and dark forest-green waistcoat; he has straight beige cotton trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather boots; a narrow dark-blue sash is tied around his waist like a functional belt, supporting a small leather case, and he wears a simple dark-brown leather shoulder satchel resting at his right hip; his overall silhouette is practical and modest, with no ostentatious insignia.
appearance.signature: Ibn Battuta’s signature prop is a worn, leather-bound travel journal held in his left hand with a reed pen tucked into the red sash, while Burt’s signature prop is a rolled paper survey map held in his right hand, secured with a thin blue cord, and the pair are always shown together with these two items visible, standing against a faint suggestion of Khajuraho’s carved temple towers in the background.

ref_desc: Ibn Battuta and T.S. Burt stand side by side, Ibn in a cream jubba with sky-blue under-tunic, deep-red sash, white turban and brown sandals holding a leather journal, Burt in khaki frock coat, beige trousers, forest-green waistcoat and brown boots holding a rolled survey map, both in cream, deep red, sky blue, khaki and brown leather tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two men standing together in a serene Khajuraho-inspired stone-temple landscape, with stylised proportions but historically grounded clothing and props: Ibn Battuta is a lean, medium-brown–skinned man in his mid-30s with an oval face, trimmed pointed beard and mustache, and sharp dark eyes, wearing a long cream-colored cotton jubba with deep-red piping over a sky-blue long-sleeved tunic and dark brown narrow trousers, a wide deep-red sash around his waist, a light gray cloak draped as a shawl, a soft white turban with a thin deep-red band, brown leather sandals, and a small belt-pouch, holding a worn leather-bound travel journal in his left hand with a reed pen tucked into his sash; beside him T.S. Burt is a slightly taller, fit light-brown–skinned man in his early 40s with an angular face, chestnut-brown hair swept back to mid-length, neatly trimmed sideburns and jawline beard, and blue-gray eyes, wearing an open light khaki cotton frock coat with brass buttons over a white shirt and dark forest-green waistcoat, straight beige trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather boots, a dark-blue sash at his waist supporting a small leather case, a dark-brown leather shoulder satchel at his right hip, and a simple tan forage cap tucked at his belt, holding a rolled paper survey map tied with blue cord; show them front-on with clear views of their outfits, colours and props, with faint, modestly carved stone temple spires in the background to evoke Khajuraho and a calm, reflective mood of shared witnessing and survival rather than triumphalism.
